title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 59
text:
135. Further information about the type of assistance which the Support Through Court or
Citizens Advice may be willing to offer can be obtained from their respective websites.
Rights of audience

136. Rights of audience are governed by Part 3 of the Legal Services Act 2007 which came into
force on 1 January 2010. This refers to the right of a non-legal representative to represent
the litigant and address the court, as opposed to simply sitting next to an LIP and assisting
as a McKenzie Friend in the traditional sense.

137. Under the Legal Services Act 2007, apart from LIPs, lay people are not allowed to conduct
litigation or act as advocates for LIPs, and LIPs are not allowed to receive or authorise such
assistance. Although courts can grant a right of audience in a particular case, the courts
have in the past been cautious, although they have been more flexible since the advent of
the Civil Procedure Rules (CPR).
